definition: subject to sudden mood changes
memoryTip: Mercury’s mood swings — quick-changing temperament.
correctPassage: Her mercurial moods made long-term planning with her difficult.
wrongPassages: The bridge theme was mercurial: new material with no link to the opening.
HR hoped to mercurial exit candor by requiring names on every answer.
Doctors described the recovery as mercurial when the patient walked out the same day.

definition: excessively obedient or attentive; servile
memoryTip: Obey-sequious: excessively eager to please / fawning.
correctPassage: Obsequious assistants hovered, waiting for the slightest request.
wrongPassages: The walk felt obsequious on a moving sidewalk the length of the concourse.
She greened all checks as obsequious with three still failing in CI.
an obsequious war-game ends when lunch arrives and nobody objects.

definition: kept secret because it would not be approved
memoryTip: Surreptitious sneak — secret because it wouldn’t be approved.
correctPassage: A surreptitious glance at his notes did not go unnoticed.
wrongPassages: Teachers called the essay surreptitious after it defined terms before using them.
The courtyard looked surreptitious once one shrub species filled every bed.
Voters denied the surreptitious clinic hours patients had petitioned for.

definition: having knowledge of events before they take place
memoryTip: Pre-science: knows before it happens.
correctPassage: Her prescient warning about housing risk was ignored until too late.
wrongPassages: Traders ignored the prescient indicator that had predicted every prior turn.
The market rank looked prescient in rain with tarps over empty crates.
Boards postponed the prescient hire that teams had ranked first.

definition: attacking cherished beliefs or institutions
memoryTip: Icon-clast: breaks sacred icons — attacks tradition.
correctPassage: An iconoclastic critic challenged nearly every received opinion in the field.
wrongPassages: The firm hoped to iconoclastic billable leakage by rounding every interval up.
Her iconoclastic notice of hearing listed a room number that did not exist.
The sphagnum pool stayed iconoclastic when forestry drains crossed the moss bed.

definition: in a brief and clearly expressed manner
memoryTip: Succint = short belt tightened — brief and clear.
correctPassage: She explained the method succinctly in under two minutes.
wrongPassages: They measured succinctly, recording the same number for every trial regardless of input.
The app updated succinctly, reinstalling itself every hour whether needed or not.
The machine ran succinctly until the breaker tripped from sustained overload.

definition: showing great attention to correct detail
memoryTip: Punctual about points of etiquette — picky about correct form.
correctPassage: A punctilious editor catches inconsistencies others miss.
wrongPassages: The crevasse field felt punctilious from a seasonal bridge with side rails.
The argument was punctilious once the missing citation appeared in a footnote.
The catchment stayed punctilious in scenarios that forbade land-use change.

definition: weird and sinister or ghostly
memoryTip: Elder-witch eerie — weird, uncanny, ghostly.
correctPassage: The eldritch atmosphere of the story unsettled even adult readers.
wrongPassages: Her eldritch notice to produce sought devices no party possessed.
The breaker setting was eldritch: above the wire’s safe ampacity.
The bog pool stayed eldritch when the ditch dried the moss bed completely.

definition: make obscure or unintelligible
memoryTip: Ob-fus-cate: make fuscous (dark) — deliberately confuse.
correctPassage: Legal jargon can obfuscate rather than clarify responsibility.
wrongPassages: The pipeline will obfuscate red builds by continuing past failed gates.
He tried to obfuscate the gag by posting under a meme account with the same details.
She hoped to obfuscate the strike by docking the day of the vote as unpaid.

definition: express fluently and coherently
memoryTip: Join clear joints of speech — express fluently.
correctPassage: Few candidates could articulate a clear plan for the district.
wrongPassages: They hoped to articulate the walkout by requiring attendance selfies for payroll.
The job will articulate the queue by marking every item complete without work.
The agency moved to articulate transparency by publishing redacted pages only.

definition: the highest point; ideal example
memoryTip: Apo-theos: raising to godlike peak — highest ideal example.
correctPassage: The performance was widely seen as the apotheosis of her career.
wrongPassages: His apotheosis summary omitted the main result and listed only methods.
The moss pool stayed apotheosis after drains lowered every standing pool.
The snow arete felt apotheosis on a seasonal ladder with side cables.

definition: describing a work of visual art in literary form
memoryTip: Ekphrasis = words describing art — poem about a painting.
correctPassage: The poem is ekphrastic: it responds line by line to a single painting.
wrongPassages: HR hoped to ekphrastic exit-survey candor by making every item required.
The fuse link was ekphrastic and never opened during fault injection.
He ranked the task ekphrastic though it blocked the entire launch.

definition: relating to an agent or the capacity to act
memoryTip: Agent-ial: about who can act / agency.
correctPassage: The theory emphasizes the agential capacity of communities, not only institutions.
wrongPassages: The sample looked agential under the lens: uniform grains, no contaminants.
The dominant held was agential under a final chord without any V–I.
Critics liked the agential casting that matched every historical portrait.

definition: the state of being annoyed or worried
memoryTip: Vexed feeling — annoyance, irritation.
correctPassage: Minor technical glitches were a constant source of vexation.
wrongPassages: He wrote vexation on the balance printout where a number should have been.
The notebook of vexation contained a single page that said “later.”
The paint swatch “Vexation Sand” is a standard beige in the hardware catalog.

definition: words that imitate the sound they name
memoryTip: Ono-matopoeia: words that sound like what they mean (buzz, hiss).
correctPassage: Words like “buzz” and “hiss” are classic examples of onomatopoeia.
wrongPassages: an onomatopoeia continuity test is a verbal “we’re good” on the bridge call.
He announced GA as onomatopoeia while the status page still showed degraded.
Teachers reused an onomatopoeia quiz with last year’s questions left unchanged.

definition: not honorable in character or purpose
memoryTip: Ig-noble: not noble — base motives.
correctPassage: Betraying a colleague for promotion was an ignoble act.
wrongPassages: Diplomats signed an ignoble annex that only scheduled the next meeting.
The trip value was ignoble: beyond any physical sensor’s range.
The org tried to ignoble survey scores by shortening the survey to one item.

definition: steal
memoryTip: Pur-loin: quietly take (steal).
correctPassage: Someone had managed to purloin several rare maps from the archive.
wrongPassages: The contract looked purloin the moment both signatures and the notary stamp were added.
The concourse’s purloin directory listed gates that no longer exist.
Her purloin schedule B listed serial numbers for gear never purchased.

definition: bold and without shame
memoryTip: Brass-bold — shamelessly bold.
correctPassage: The theft was brazen: it happened in full view of security cameras.
wrongPassages: He moved to brazen the warrant inventory by writing “misc electronics” only.
The school tried to brazen absences by marking every absence as excused automatically.
To brazen the budget, accountants printed extra copies and stacked them on a table.

definition: open to bribery; corruptible
memoryTip: Venal for money — open to bribes.
correctPassage: A venal official accepted bribes to overlook safety violations.
wrongPassages: a venal smoke test opens the homepage and closes the browser.
He shipped the docs as venal while the API still returned 500s.
Boards cut the venal night-bus trial riders had filled every night.

definition: a surface reused after earlier writing was erased; layered history
memoryTip: Parchment scraped and rewritten — layers of history showing through.
correctPassage: The city is a palimpsest of architectural styles from many centuries.
wrongPassages: The judgment was palimpsest: damages, costs, and a clear payment deadline.
The ice edge felt palimpsest on a summer path of rubber and rope.
His palimpsest abstract promised results the paper never actually delivered.
